```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import wade
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "tools"))
import tcga_examples as TC
from notebook_support import output_dir, markdown_table, export_table
OUT = output_dir("breast")
cohort = TC.load_cohort("breast", OUT)
PANEL = TC.BREAST_PANEL
SHOW = ["gene","case_mean","control_mean","area_fraction","area_padj","subset_fraction","subset_log2fc","subset_padj"]
def table(frame,name):
    markdown_table(frame,OUT,name)
```

## Prespecified design

Use full **gene counts** and one library per patient and sample class. The
primary unpaired comparison retains eligible normal-adjacent samples and
excludes their paired tumours, leaving independent patients. Technical and
population exclusions are fixed before gene testing; cases are not removed
because they weaken a signal. Exact retained IDs and exclusions are exported.

RLE is fitted on the full measured gene universe after primary sample selection.
The prespecified example test mask requires at least 10 counts in five pooled
samples and pooled mean CPM at least 0.1, using the eligible input cohort.
This is an example recipe, not a universal threshold. Test filtering reuses
the fitted factors. The area test runs on counts thinned binomially to the
shallowest library's depth; the subset test uses normalized counts with WADE's
seeded count jitter, `(count + jitter) / size_factor`; figures use log2. Repeated observations, depth and tissue mixture remain relevant to
interpretation. The upstream count processing/reference record remains a
release documentation requirement.

```{python}
#| label: accounting
#| output: asis
primary_meta = cohort.meta[cohort.independent.tolist()]
table(primary_meta.group_by("group").len(),"primary-accounting")
```

## Whole-transcriptome tests

Each gene's area and subset are tested with the default settings (both
directions, `pvalues="auto"`, `relative_error=0.2`, the
999,999-shuffle budget, seed 1), and each test has one BH family over the
tested genes. Display markers were fixed in advance; their inclusion does not
imply significance.

```{python}
#| label: primary
#| output: false
res = TC.run(cohort,cohort.independent,OUT,"primary")
annotation_values = TC.annotation_expression(cohort,res,PANEL)
export_table(annotation_values,OUT,"panel-expression-annotations")
```

```{python}
#| label: transcriptome-calls
#| output: asis
area,subset=res.area_padj<=.05,res.subset_padj<=.05
table(pl.DataFrame({"Tested genes":[int(res.tested.sum())],
    "Area up":[int(np.sum(area&(res.area>0)))],"Area down":[int(np.sum(area&(res.area<0)))],
    "Subset above":[int(np.sum(subset&(res.subset_side=="up")))],"Subset below":[int(np.sum(subset&(res.subset_side=="down")))]}),
    "transcriptome-calls")
```

These broad call sets require review of the normalization reference, tissue
mixture and technical effects. Marker recovery does not establish their
real-data false discovery proportion.

## Breast subtypes

PAM50 subtype labels are expression-derived and illustrate biology; recovery
of subtype markers is not independent validation. HER2-enriched is not
synonymous with clinical HER2 positivity, and basal-like is not synonymous
with triple-negative disease. Unknown and normal-like labels remain separate.
The [TCGA breast study](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature11412) and the
frozen cBioPortal annotations describe the source. DNA copy-number calls and
clinical receptor assays provide complementary measurements, not a new cohort.

```{python}
#| label: subtype-coverage
#| output: asis
table(primary_meta.filter(pl.col("group")=="tumor").group_by("subtype").len().sort("subtype"),"subtype-coverage")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-erbb2
#| fig-cap: "ERBB2 distributions and quantile effects in the independent primary tumour-versus-normal comparison."
res.plot_gene("ERBB2")
```

ERBB2's subset was found without labels. The PanCancer GISTIC calls, which
WADE never sees, mark high-level amplification (category 2); tumours with any
other call count as negatives and missing calls are excluded.

```{python}
#| label: erbb2-subset
#| output: asis
amplified={g:("ERBB2_CNA",2,{-2,-1,0,1}) for g in ["ERBB2","GRB7"]}
table(TC.annotated_subsets(cohort,res,amplified),"erbb2-subset")
```

Most tumours express ERBB2 and GRB7 somewhat above the normals, and the
amplified tumours sit higher still. The area carries the broad rise; the
subset is what departs from the fold most tumours share.

```{python}
#| label: fig-subtypes
#| fig-cap: "Tested expression by supplied subtype, on log2. Points are spread horizontally for display."
groups=["Normal-adjacent"]+TC.SUBTYPES+["Normal-like","Unknown"]
labels=np.where(primary_meta["group"].to_numpy()=="normal","Normal-adjacent",primary_meta["subtype"].to_numpy())
colors=["#7d8790","#4b9e9a","#6986b5","#bd556f","#b58b3b","#9f80b0","#c1c5ca"]
fig,axes=plt.subplots(2,3,figsize=(11,7),layout="constrained")
rng=np.random.default_rng(17)
for ax,gene in zip(axes.flat,["ERBB2","GRB7","ESR1","PGR","KRT5","MKI67"]):
    values=TC.log2_expression(res,gene)
    for j,(group,color) in enumerate(zip(groups,colors)):
        v=values[labels==group]
        if len(v):
            ax.scatter(j+rng.uniform(-.17,.17,len(v)),v,s=5,alpha=.3,color=color,linewidths=0)
            ax.boxplot([v],positions=[j],widths=.4,showfliers=False,boxprops={"color":color})
    ax.set(title=gene,xticks=range(len(groups)),xticklabels=groups,ylabel="log₂(normalized count + 1)")
    ax.tick_params(axis="x",labelrotation=65,labelsize=8)
fig
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Prespecified tumour-subtype contrasts

Compare each of the four named subtypes with the other three, excluding
normal-like and unknown from these contrasts while retaining their accounting
above. The tumour reference fit is frozen before the contrasts. Each contrast
uses the same eligible genes and seed, with a prespecified 99,999-shuffle
budget. For each test, one BH correction covers every gene × contrast p-value
together. This is an exploratory expression-label association family, not
independent validation of PAM50. With the shuffled floor of 10⁻⁵, a subset
discovery in this family needs several genes at the floor together.

```{python}
#| label: subtype-tests
#| output: false
subtype_idx=np.flatnonzero(((cohort.meta["group"]=="tumor") & cohort.meta["subtype"].is_in(TC.SUBTYPES)).to_numpy())
subtype_names=cohort.meta["subtype"].to_numpy()[subtype_idx]
contrasts={name:TC.run(cohort,subtype_idx,OUT,"subtype-"+str(j),
                      condition=(subtype_names==name).astype(int),reference="subtypes",max_permutations=99_999)
           for j,name in enumerate(TC.SUBTYPES)}
q={test:wade.bh_adjust(np.concatenate([getattr(r,test+"_pvalue") for r in contrasts.values()])).reshape(len(contrasts),-1)
   for test in ("area","subset")}
frames=[]
for j,(name,r) in enumerate(contrasts.items()):
    frames.append(r.to_frame().with_columns(subtype=pl.lit(name),q_area_four_contrasts=pl.Series(q["area"][j]),
                                            q_subset_four_contrasts=pl.Series(q["subset"][j])))
all_contrasts=pl.concat(frames)
export_table(all_contrasts,OUT,"all-subtype-contrasts")
```

```{python}
#| label: subtype-panel
#| output: asis
table(all_contrasts.filter(pl.col("gene").is_in(["ERBB2","ESR1","KRT5","MKI67"])).select(
    "subtype","gene","area_fraction","subset_fraction","subset_log2fc","q_area_four_contrasts","q_subset_four_contrasts"),"subtype-panel")
```
